flags.reason: The guide (checked 20 October on 0.1.78-c7d3348) still describes Component Bug #355 problems that the installed 0.1.78-dbe0e02 fixes, read from source: the description is readable (card/supportive-text/color, #1a1c1f in every Text Appearance mode, not the white text/appearance/medium/color), the picture sits in a 288 px centred frame instead of filling the card’s width, and the name (1 line) and description (2 lines) end in … unless disableTruncation is set. The entry follows the package, so it does not say “white on white” or “disableTruncation affects only the stats”. The guide changes when #355 is closed and published. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch7, for Marcin to confirm.

examples.purpose: A gold coin's product page, the guide's In context: the overview explains the product, and the Buy button under it belongs to the screen, because the card has no action of its own; Buy opens the screen's own checkout. The image URIs stand for the product's own picture and the brand's logo.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <ProductOverview
    imageSource={{ uri: 'https://example.com/gold-coin.png' }}
    labelImageSource={{ uri: 'https://example.com/jio-gold-logo.png' }}
    label="Gold"
    productName="5g Gold Coin"
    description="Your gold is insured from our vault to you. If lost or damaged, we’ll replace it."
    stats={[
      { value: '995', label: 'Purity' },
      { value: '3%', label: 'GST' },
    ]}
  />
  <Button label="Buy for ₹38,750" onPress={() => {}} />
</VStack>

from.quote: The overview explains the product; the Buy button under it belongs to the screen, because the card has no action of its own.

props.name: imageSource
props.description: Hero image source rendered at the top of the card.

props.name: imageRatio
props.description: Aspect ratio for the hero image. Defaults to the Figma frame (288:170). Default 1.6941 (FIGMA_IMAGE_WIDTH / FIGMA_IMAGE_HEIGHT), from the component source.

props.name: labelImageSource
props.description: Avatar source for the inline ProductLabel chip.

props.name: label
props.description: The chip always shows; label defaults to “Gold”. Declared: Text shown next to the avatar in the ProductLabel chip. Default "Gold", from the component source.

props.name: productName
props.description: The name is a header (accessibilityRole header; an h1 on the web), centred. Declared: The large product name, e.g. "0.5g Gold Coin". Default "0.5g Gold Coin", from the component source.

props.name: description
props.default: Your gold is insured from our vault to you. If lost or damaged, we’ll replace it.
props.description: The short multi-line description below the product name. Default "Your gold is insured from our vault to you. If lost or damaged, we’ll replace it.", from the component source.

props.name: stats
props.description: Each stat is an equal column (flex 1): a 20 px heavy value over a 12 px label, each on one line ending in … unless disableTruncation is set. Declared: Stats rendered in the bottom row. Each stat shows a large value above a smaller label. Pass an empty array (or `null`) to hide the row.

props.name: modes
props.description: Design token modes for theming (e.g. `{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }`).

props.name: children
props.description: Custom slot rendered between the description and the stats row, useful for badges, callouts, etc. Receives the same `modes` as the parent and is centred with the rest of the card.

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, the product name and description wrap instead of ellipsizing. By default the name is one line and the description is at most two.

gaps.text: The name's line is 32 px where Figma's is 26, and a stat value's 24 where Figma's is 20, so the card is taller than Figma's 396 px (Component Bug #355).
Left out, imageSource and labelImageSource give no picture and no chip picture, where Figma's component shows the coin and the Jio dot.
Figma's Product Overview has no properties: the picture, chip, text, and two stats are layers there.
Figma has no children, imageRatio or disableTruncation, and its frame holds a fixed two stats; the package takes any number of stats.
The published Storybook is older than the installed package and still shows the older generated page (Component Bug #355).
